summary: A Quote subscription on a CDS future: Kite's currency prices are in 10^-7 rupees, so the desktop's frame carries USDINR at 88.1234; the web divides by 100.

notes: Kite documents the divisor per segment: 10^7 for CDS, 10^4 for BCD, 100 otherwise; the low byte of the instrument token is the segment.

deviations.reason: Kite sends currency derivative prices in units of 10^-7 rupees (BCD 10^-4); the web divides every price by 100, so USDINR at 88.1234 reaches clients as 8812340.0. The desktop divides by the segment's unit (brokers/zerodha/streaming.rs parse_packet).
deviations.ref: zerodha_websocket.py:718-793; audit WEBSOCKET_AUDIT_PRIMARY_BROKERS.md, 'Zerodha Rust corrects existing web parser defects'
